God hath revealed his will to me in a vision, or a dream.</ns0:note>, and an embassador is sent unto the heathen <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">He speaks after the manner of earthly Princes, who use to send their Em<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bassadors to other Princes to declare their minds to them. The meaning is God hath made such impressions upon other Nations, he hath inclined them, or set them on work, to get together in Armies to come against <ns0:hi>Edom</ns0:hi> in Battel.</ns0:note>, <ns0:hi>say<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing,</ns0:hi> Gather ye together, and come against her, and rise to the battel <ns0:hi>r.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 For lo, I will make thee small amongst the heathen, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> despised among men <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Obadiah</ns0:hi> in his prophesie against <ns0:hi>Edom, ver.</ns0:hi> 2. hath much the same words importing that God would bring the <ns0:hi>Edomites</ns0:hi> ve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ry low, and make them very contemptible.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 Thy terribleness hath deceived thee, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> the pride of thy heart <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Obadiah</ns0:hi> in his Prophesie against <ns0:hi>Edom</ns0:hi> useth much the same expressions, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 3, 4. the word that is here used being of the number of those which are but once found in Scripture hath given Interpreters liberty to abound in their senses of it; some tran<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />slating it <ns0:hi>Arrogance,</ns0:hi> some, thine <ns0:hi>Idol,</ns0:hi> but the best Interpreters understand by it their terribleness to others, their being so potent that others were all afraid of them, this deceived them, making them to conclude themselves secure, and out of danger. To which is also added the <ns0:hi>pride</ns0:hi> of the heart.</ns0:note>, O thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">The Countrey of <ns0:hi>Edom</ns0:hi> being mountainous they are said to dwell in the clefts of the Rocks, that is in places impregnable, and inaccessible as they thought in the heights of the hill.</ns0:note>, that holdest the height of the hill; though thou shouldest make thy nest as high as the eagle, I will bring thee down from thence, saith the LORD <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">But the Lord lets them know no place was to his power inaccessible or impregnable, for if they dwell as high as the Eagle which the Scripture tells us <ns0:hi>Iob</ns0:hi> 39.27, 28. <ns0:hi>Maketh her nest on high, and dwelleth and abideth upon the rock, upon the crag of the rock,</ns0:hi> yet he would bring them down.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 Also Edom shall be a desolation: every one that goeth by it, shall be astonished, and shall hiss at all the plagues thereof <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">The like is said of <ns0:hi>Babylon, chap.</ns0:hi> 50.13. it appears from 1 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 9.8. that it was a kind of <ns0:hi>Proverbial expression,</ns0:hi> when they would express a great desolation, or great plagues, that those who passed by such a place, should <ns0:hi>be astonished,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>hiss at it.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Gen. 19.25. Deut. 29.23. Amos 4.11.</ns0:note> As in the overthrow of Sodom and Go<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />morrah and the neighbour <ns0:hi>cities</ns0:hi> thereof, saith the LORD: no man shall abide there, neither shall a son of man dwell in it <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Sodom</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Gomorrah,</ns0:hi> and the Neighbour Cities were utterly destroyed, and therefore are set down both here and <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 50.40. as patterns of an utter ruine and desolation.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 50.44.</ns0:note> Behold, he shall come up like a lion from thee <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 12.5.</ns0:note> swelling of Jordan, against the habitation of the strong <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">This verse is very variously interpreted, some by <ns0:hi>he</ns0:hi> under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stand the <ns0:hi>Iews,</ns0:hi> some understand <ns0:hi>Nebuchadnezzar,</ns0:hi> some under<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stand the <ns0:hi>Edomites,</ns0:hi> I think the last is most probable to be here meant, because of the next words. The <ns0:hi>Edomites</ns0:hi> shall come out against the <ns0:hi>Caldeans, like a Lion,</ns0:hi> as Lions lurking about <ns0:hi>Iordan</ns0:hi> when it overfloweth, come out to take their prey.</ns0:note>: but I will suddenly make him run away from her <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">These words are variously understood, those who by <ns0:hi>he</ns0:hi> in the former part of the verse understand <ns0:hi>Nebuchadnezzar,</ns0:hi> interpret the run<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ning here mentioned, of his running over the whole Countrey of <ns0:hi>Edom,</ns0:hi> to me it appeareth a much more probable sense to inter<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pret it of the <ns0:hi>Edomites</ns0:hi> running away from <ns0:hi>Nebuchadnezzar</ns0:hi> out of their own Country, which seems to be understood <ns0:hi>by her,</ns0:hi> all that makes a difficulty is the particle <ns0:hi>from,</ns0:hi> which yet makes the sense good enough, if by <ns0:hi>her</ns0:hi> we understand the <ns0:hi>Edomites</ns0:hi> own Land. In the <ns0:hi>Hebrew</ns0:hi> it is <ns0:hi>I will break them,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>I will quiet them,</ns0:hi> and make them <ns0:hi>to run.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>, and who <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> a chosen <ns0:hi>man that</ns0:hi> I may appoint over her <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">Whom shall I set over <ns0:hi>Edom</ns0:hi>? into whose hands shall I give that Countrey that he may rule over it?</ns0:note>? for <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 15.11. Job 41.10.</ns0:note> who <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> like me <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">For I can do whatsoever I please.</ns0:note>? and who will <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>convent me in judgment.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> 
                  <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Exod. 15.11. Job 41.10.</ns0:note> appoint me the time? and who <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> that shepherd that will stand before me <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">What is that King or Potentate of the Earth that will stand before me?</ns0:note>?<ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">And who will appoint me a time to plead with men, so <ns0:hi>Iob</ns0:hi> 9.19. or a time to fight.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 Therefore hear the counsel of the LORD, that he hath taken against Edom, and his purposes that he hath purposed against the inhabitants of Teman <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Edom</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Teman</ns0:hi> in this verse signifie both the same thing, God calls to men to hear the resolutions he had taken up against the <ns0:hi>Edomites,</ns0:hi> resolutions as wise and steady as if they had been taken upon the wisest counsels, and deliberation.</ns0:note>: Surely the least of the flock shall draw them out <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">God is re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />solved to drive out the <ns0:hi>Edomites,</ns0:hi> and the least of <ns0:hi>Nebuchadnezzar</ns0:hi>'s Forces shall drag them out of their lurking places, and God will make the place where they dwell a desolation.</ns0:note>, surely, he shall make their habitations desolate with them <ns0:hi>g.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 The earth is moved at the noise of their fall: at the cry, the noise thereof was heard in the <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>wee<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>y Sea.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> Red-sea <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">That is, the ruine of the <ns0:hi>Edomites</ns0:hi> shall be so great, that all nations round about it shall be affected at the noise of their fall and though the <ns0:hi>Red-Sea,</ns0:hi> or the weedy Sea be at a great distance from them, yet their noise shall reach thither.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 Behold, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 4.1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> he shall come up and flie as the eagle, and spread his wings over Bozrah: and at that day shall the heart of the mighty men of E<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dom be as the heart of a woman in her pangs <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">See the Notes on <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 48.40, 41. where the very same thing, and under the same phrases, was spoken against <ns0:hi>Moab.</ns0:hi> That which is threatned is the Enemies coming swiftly upon the <ns0:hi>Edom<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ites</ns0:hi> and preying upon them, and the fear that should surprize them which should make their hearts faint as the heart of a wo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />man that hath an hard labour.</ns0:note>:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 ¶ <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Zech. 9.12<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  </ns0:note> Concerning Damascus <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">The Prophet comes to denounce the judgments of God against <ns0:hi>Syria,</ns0:hi> another nation of the Gentiles, <ns0:hi>Damascus</ns0:hi> was the head City of <ns0:hi>Syria, Isa.</ns0:hi> 7.8. and 17.3. or <ns0:hi>Aram</ns0:hi> (as in the <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi>) because it was a Country inhabited by the posterity of <ns0:hi>Aram</ns0:hi> one of the sons of <ns0:hi>Sem,</ns0:hi> part of it lay betwixt <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Arabia,</ns0:hi> and was called <ns0:hi>Mesopotamia,</ns0:hi> lying betwixt the two Rivers of <ns0:hi>Tigris</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Eu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phrates. Laban</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Naaman</ns0:hi> were of this Countrey, <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> had War with them 2 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 8.5. and 10.18. So had <ns0:hi>Ahab</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>King.</ns0:hi> 20.20. and <ns0:hi>Ioram</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 8.28. And <ns0:hi>Aha<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> Isai.</ns0:hi> 7.2. after Gods long patience with them he threatens them with ruine, as by <ns0:hi>Ieremiah</ns0:hi> in this place, so by <ns0:hi>Amos</ns0:hi> 1.5. <ns0:hi>Damascus</ns0:hi> being the head City of this Country is sometimes put (as here) for the whole Countrey.</ns0:note>. Hamath is confounded, and Arpad <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Hamath</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Arpad</ns0:hi> were two Cities also of <ns0:hi>Sy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ria,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 18.34.</ns0:note>: for they have heard evil tidings, they are <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                        <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  </ns0:note> faint-hearted, <ns0:hi>there is</ns0:hi> sor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />row <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>as <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                           <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> Sea.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> on the sea, it cannot be quiet <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">The Prophet foretels that they also should hear of ill news, an Enemy that is coming against them, and that they should be melted through fear, and their courage should fail them, they should be as troubled as the Sea is in a storm, or their inhabitants that lived near to the Sea should be troubled.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Syria</ns0:hi> whose head is <ns0:hi>Damascus</ns0:hi> hath lost her old courage and valour; it was wont to be a formidable Country to its Neigh<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bours.</ns0:note> Damascus is waxed feeble, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> turneth her self to flee <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">But now they flee before their Enemies.</ns0:note>, and fear hath seized on <ns0:hi>her</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">They are seized, and overpowred by their own fears.</ns0:note>: <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 4.3<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>. and 30.6.</ns0:note> an<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />guish and sorrowes have taken her, as a woman in travail <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Great sorrows are ordinarily in Scripture expressed by the similitude of the pains of a woman in travail, we have met with it often in this Prophesie, <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 6.24. and 22.23. so <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 48.6. <ns0:hi>Micah</ns0:hi> 4.9.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 How is the city of praise not left, the city of my joy <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">It is called the City of praise, because it was a City so much praised, a City of great renown, which the Prophet seeing like to be destroyed, lamenteth either in the person of the <ns0:hi>King of Sy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ria,</ns0:hi> or of the <ns0:hi>Syrian Inhabitants,</ns0:hi> wondering that the conquerours should not spare so famous and renowned a Ci<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>y in which so ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ny did rejoyce.</ns0:note>?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">26 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 50 <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> Therefore her young men shall fall in her streets, and all the men of war shall be cut off in that day, saith the LORD of hosts <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>Hebrew particles</ns0:hi> are not always well rendred in our Transla<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion, and our Learned English <ns0:hi>Annotator</ns0:hi> hath rightly observed this place, as one instance, for <ns0:gap reason="foreign">
                        <ns0:desc>〈 in non-Latin alphabet 〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> cannot be here an illative, but is much better translated <ns0:hi>surely</ns0:hi> as a note of assertion. God threat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />neth the <ns0:hi>Syrians</ns0:hi> with a certain ruine, and desolation.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:61" />27 And I will kindle a fire in the wall of Da<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mascus <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">I will bring a judgment that shall burn in <ns0:hi>Damascus</ns0:hi> like a con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />suming Fire, and it shall reach to the Royal seat of <ns0:hi>Benhadad,</ns0:hi> either that which was the Royal seat of <ns0:hi>Benhadad,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 8.7. or else <ns0:hi>Ben-hadad,</ns0:hi> (signifying the son of <ns0:hi>Hadad</ns0:hi>) (which was their Idol) was the common name of all the Kings of <ns0:hi>Syria,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Pharaoh</ns0:hi> was to the Kings of <ns0:hi>Egypt, Amos</ns0:hi> 1.4.</ns0:note>, and it shall consume the palaces of Ben<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />hadad <ns0:hi>u.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 ¶ Concerning Kedar <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Kedar, Gen.</ns0:hi> 25.13. was one of the Sons of <ns0:hi>Ishmael</ns0:hi> whose posterity inhabited part of <ns0:hi>Arabia Petraea,</ns0:hi> See <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 21.13, 17. we read of it <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 120.5. <ns0:hi>Cant.</ns0:hi> 1.5. <ns0:hi>Ezek.</ns0:hi> 27.21.</ns0:note>, and concerning the kingdoms of Hazor <ns0:note n="x" place="bottom">We read of <ns0:hi>Hazor, Iosh.</ns0:hi> 11.1. <ns0:hi>verse.</ns0:hi> 10. it was the head City to se<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />veral Kingdoms in <ns0:hi>Ioshua</ns0:hi>'s time, <ns0:hi>Ia<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>in</ns0:hi> was King of it in the times of <ns0:hi>Deborah, Iudg.</ns0:hi> 4.2.</ns0:note>, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon shall smite, thus saith the LORD <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">The Prophet foretels that <ns0:hi>Nebuchad<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nezzar</ns0:hi> should also conquer these Kingdoms.</ns0:note>, Arise ye, go up to Kedar, and spoil the men of the east <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">And saith he heard the Lord call to <ns0:hi>Nebuchadnezzar</ns0:hi> to go up against them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 Their tents and their flocks shall they take away <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">That is, the <ns0:hi>Chaldeans</ns0:hi> shall take away the <ns0:hi>Kedarens Tents,</ns0:hi> for they being a people whose Cattel, had no fixed houses but Tents which were moveable habitations, covered with skins of Beasts.</ns0:note>, they shall take to themselves their cur<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tains and all their vessels, and their camels <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">And the curtains which they used to draw before those Tents, and served them as sides, as gable ends of houses serve us, and all the furniture of their Tents or Tabernacles, and their Cattel, and either their Enemies should fright them with terrible noises and outcryes, or they should themselves cry out that they were surrounded with objects of fear.</ns0:note>, and they shall cry unto them, Fear <ns0:hi>is,</ns0:hi> on every side <ns0:hi>c.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 ¶ Flee, <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>flit greatly.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> get you far off, dwell deep, O ye inhabitants of Hazor, saith the LORD <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">The words seem to be the Prophets words of advice to this people, to make all the hast they could away, and to secure them<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />selves as well as they could because the King of <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi> had cer<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tainly been taking counsel against them, and was resolved to di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sturb them. See <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 8. where the like counsel is given to the <ns0:hi>Edomites.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
                  <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> for Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon hath taken coun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sel against you, and hath conceived a purpose a<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />gainst you <ns0:hi>e.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 Arise, get you up to the <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>the nation that is at ease.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> wealthy nation that dwelleth without care, saith the LORD, which have neither gates nor bars, <ns0:hi>which</ns0:hi> dwell alone <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">The supposed result of <ns0:hi>Nebuchadnezzars</ns0:hi> counsels, giving charge to his Armies to march against the <ns0:hi>Kedarens,</ns0:hi> which lived at ease and quiet, and took no care. That had no Cities, nor Gates, nor Barrs to keep their Enemies out, nor were near any Neigh<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bours that could assist them, nor very near to one another living in Tents, so might easily be overrun, and conquered, and made a prey to Enemies.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="32">32 And their Camels shall be a booty, and the multitude of their cattel a spoil <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">These words sound like a part of the King of <ns0:hi>Babylons</ns0:hi> suppo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sed speech incouraging his Souldiers from the booty they should get, which should be a great multitude of Camels and other Cat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tel.</ns0:note>, and I will scat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter into all winds <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 9.26. and 25.23.</ns0:note> them <ns0:hi>that are</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="†" place="margin">Heb. <ns0:hi>cut off into corners,</ns0:hi> or, <ns0:hi>that have the corners of</ns0:hi> their hair <ns0:hi>polled.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> in the utmost corners, and I will bring their calamity, from all sides thereof, saith the LORD <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">The latter words are the words of the Prophet in the name of the Lord threatning ruine to these <ns0:hi>Kedarens</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Hazorites,</ns0:hi> though they lived in corners<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and might upon that account think themselves secure, God saith, he would fetch them out of their utmost corners, and bring calamity from all parts upon them.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 And Hazor <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">chap. 10.22.</ns0:note> shall be a dwelling for dragons, <ns0:hi>and</ns0:hi> a desolation for ever; there shall no man abide there, nor <ns0:hi>any</ns0:hi> son of man dwell in it <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">That is, the whole Countrey subject to the King of <ns0:hi>Hazor,</ns0:hi> shall be desolate, see <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 34.13. <ns0:hi>chap.</ns0:hi> 9.11.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>

                     <ns0:hi>Elam</ns0:hi> was the son of <ns0:hi>Sem, Gen.</ns0:hi> 10.22. his posterity were called <ns0:hi>Ela<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                        </ns0:gap>ites,</ns0:hi> these were the <ns0:hi>Persians</ns0:hi> as is most probable, though some judge that the <ns0:hi>Persians</ns0:hi> were at too great a distance from the Jews to be the people meant here, but we read of no other <ns0:hi>Elam</ns0:hi> in Scripture but in <ns0:hi>Persia, Dan.</ns0:hi> 8.2. and though they were indeed at a great distance, yet it is probable that <ns0:hi>Nebu<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />chadnezzar</ns0:hi> having conquered the <ns0:hi>Assyrians</ns0:hi> might also make some inroads in <ns0:hi>Persia,</ns0:hi> the Emperour of which afterward conquered <ns0:hi>Babylon.</ns0:hi> This Prophesie being in the first year of <ns0:hi>Zedekiah</ns0:hi> must needs be long before the thing was done, for it was ten years be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore the King of <ns0:hi>Babylon</ns0:hi> took <ns0:hi>Hierusalem.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="35">35 Thus saith the LORD of hosts, Behold, I will break the bow of Elam, the chief of their might <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">All those Eastern people were famous for the use of the <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ow, the <ns0:hi>Elamites</ns0:hi> in special, <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 22.6. those bows were the <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> their offensive armour, though by <ns0:hi>the chief of their mi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>
                     </ns0:hi> may also be meant their most mighty and strong Warriours. This Prophesie is probably judged to be fulfilled when the <ns0:hi>Persians</ns0:hi> made a defection from the King of the <ns0:hi>Medes</ns0:hi> who was son in Law to <ns0:hi>Nebuchadnezzar.</ns0:hi> Others think that this Prophesie was accom<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plished by <ns0:hi>Alexander</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Emperour</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Greece,</ns0:hi> or rather by his Suc<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cessors.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="36">36 And upon Elam will I bring the four winds, from the four quarters of heaven, and will scat<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter them towards all those winds; and there shall be no nation whither the outcasts of Elam shall not come <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">The Prophet threatneth the destruction of the <ns0:hi>Persians,</ns0:hi> by a Confederacy of Enemies, suppose <ns0:hi>Babylonians, Medes,</ns0:hi> &c. which should assault them on all sides, as when the wind blows at the same time from all quarters, which causeth a whirlwind which driveth the dust every way hither<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and thither, so he saith the <ns0:hi>Persians</ns0:hi> should be scattered into all nations.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="37">37 For I will cause Elam to be dismayed before their enemies, and before them that seek their life: and I will bring evil upon them, <ns0:hi>even</ns0:hi> my fierce anger, saith the LORD, and I will send the sword after them, till I have consumed them <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">We met with the like threatnings, <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 5, 24, 29. as to <ns0:hi>fear,</ns0:hi> and as to their destruction we have often met with the like threatnings.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 And I will set my throne in Elam <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">God here calls the throne of <ns0:hi>Nebuchadnezzar,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Cyrus,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Alex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ander</ns0:hi> (who ever he was that conquered the <ns0:hi>Persians</ns0:hi>) his throne. 1. Because God gave it the Conquerour. 2. Or, because God shewed himself the Lord of hosts, or the Lord of the whole Earth, by disposing the Kingdom of <ns0:hi>Persia</ns0:hi> at his pleasure.</ns0:note>, and will destroy from thence the king and the princes, saith the LORD <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">He doth not threaten the destruction of the whole Nation, but the making of it all Tributary, so as it should have no Kings nor Princes of its own.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="39">39 ¶ But it shall come to pass in the latter dayes, <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> I will bring again the captivity of Elam, saith the LORD <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">We had the like promise as to <ns0:hi>Moah, chap.</ns0:hi> 48.47. and as to <ns0:hi>Ammon ver.</ns0:hi> 6. the same latter dayes either signifie after many dayes, or in the time of the <ns0:hi>Messias.</ns0:hi> In the former sense it may refer to <ns0:hi>Cyrus,</ns0:hi> who conquered <ns0:hi>Persia.</ns0:hi> In the latter sense it is re<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ferred to the spiritual liberty which some of these poor heathens were brought into by the Gospel, we read <ns0:hi>Act.</ns0:hi> 2.9. that some of these <ns0:hi>Elamites</ns0:hi> were at <ns0:hi>Hierusalem</ns0:hi> at <ns0:hi>Pentecost,</ns0:hi> and were some of those converted to Christ.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
